163.title: Applications open for MESC 2026
163.text:
PBS CEO Keith Chetcuti announced that the semi-finals of the Malta Eurovision Song Contest will take place on 15 January, while the final will be on 17 January.
PBS will publish the rules for singers or groups to participate in this festival from today. Song submissions will be accepted from 17 – 23 November.
Mr Chetcuti explained that on 1 December, the 18 semi-finalists will be announced who will then take part in the semi-final on 15 January.
In that semi-final, through the votes of the jury and also of the public, the 12 finalists for the final evening on 17 January will be voted on.
The winner or winners will then represent Malta in the Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna next May. This will be the 70th edition of the Eurovision Song Contest.

418.title: Malta’s Search Begins: Submissions for Malta Eurovision Song Contest 2026 Now Open
418.text:
Public Broadcasting Services Limited (PBS) has officially opened the submission window for the Malta Eurovision Song Contest (MESC) 2026. Artists, authors, and composers are invited to submit their original entries for consideration.
The submission window is open from 17 November 2025 and will close at 23:59 CET on 23 November 2025. All entries must be submitted electronically via the official website https://maltaeurovision.mt/submissions/.
Following the submission deadline, the contest will proceed with several key dates. The announcement of the Semi-Finalists is scheduled for 01 December 2025. The live televised Semi-Final will take place on 15 January 2026, followed shortly by the MESC Grand Final on 17 January 2026.
PBS encourages all interested artists, authors, and composers to review the complete MESC 2026 Regulations, available on the official website, before submitting an entry.

489.title: Submissions Locked Down: Malta’s Search for Eurovision 2026 Moves to Selection Phase
489.text:
The excitement is mounting as the official song submission period for the Malta Eurovision Song Contest (MESC) 2026 has concluded! PBS is now sifting through the entries in its search for the artist and song that will represent the nation at the 70th Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna, Austria, next May.
The selection process is clearly defined, promising two nights of thrilling live music competition in January 2026.
The next crucial milestone is less than a week away:
Monday, December 1, 2025: The highly anticipated list of the 18 Semi-Finalists and their corresponding songs will be officially announced by PBS.

1006.title: AIDAN taking ‘Bella’ to Bulgaria
1006.text:
AIDAN, Malta’s representative for the Eurovsion Song Contest 2026 with the winning song ‘Bella’, will travel to Bulgaria on Friday to take part in their national final. The Balkan country will be voting in Malta’s semi-final on 14th May.
Bulgaria is the first country in which AIDAN will perform ‘Bella’ on stage following his victory, kicking off a busy and unforgettable Eurovision journey.
On Saturday morning AIDAN will appear on the most watched morning show in Bulgaria, “This Morning’ on the BNT channel, and will have interviews on television and radio in the following days until his return to Malta. All this to continue promoting the song ‘Bella’. The evening where AIDAN will give his performance will take place on Saturday evening, 31 January,
“I’m really looking forward to visiting Bulgaria again; the last time I was here, I recorded ‘Bella’ with the Bulgarian Symphony Orchestra last November. I’m also looking forward to meeting Alis, Albania’s Eurovision representative who will also be singing as a special guest. ”
AIDAN

918.title: Aidan wins Malta Eurovision Song Contest
918.text:
Aidan has won this year’s edition of the Maltese Eurovision Song Contest with the song “Bella” which acquired 283 points.
In second place was MATT BLXCK with the song “Ejja Lejja Ħdejja ‘l Hawn (The Flute)” which gained 268 points with Mychael Bartolo Chircop in third place with “My Sweet Angel” who acquired 136 points.
In yesterday’s final session following Thursday’s semi-final, the 12 finalists competed for the honour to represent Malta on the international stage in the coming weeks.
The semi-final and final were held in the Ċentru tal-Fieri u l-Konferenzi at MFCC in Ta’ Qali.
Aidan will represent Malta in the Eurovision Song Contest of this year to be held in Vienna in Austria between 12th and 16th May.
He will sing in the second part on 14th May following the draw carried out in recent days.

649.title: Nathan Psaila – Ganador
649.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Nathan Psaila delivered a dramatic and powerful conclusion to the night with “Ganador.” Closing the show on January 15, Psaila captivated the audience with a fierce, fiery performance that lived up to its title, “Winner.” His vocal delivery was commanding, navigating the song’s intense emotional arc with professional precision. The staging featured high-impact visual elements that emphasized the anthem’s grand energy.
Having successfully qualified for the Grand Final on January 17, Nathan will be the fifth artist to perform. His entry stands out for its raw determination and modern, high-stakes competitive spirit.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

655.title: Mychael Bartolo Chircop – My Sweet Angel
655.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Mychael Bartolo Chircop enchanted the audience as the contest’s youngest participant with his entry, “My Sweet Angel.” His performance featured a gentle, acoustic-leaning style that highlighted his “stunning voice” and emotional sincerity. On stage at the MFCC, the staging employed a simple yet effective approach, utilizing light to focus entirely on his vocal delivery.
Having successfully qualified for the Grand Final on January 17, Mychael will be the eighth artist to perform. His unique contribution lies in his youthful, sweet-natured energy, offering a heartfelt and intimate contrast to the night’s high-tempo tracks.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

661.title: Matthew and The Afterparty – Brutality Mentality
661.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Matthew Cilia & The AfterParty brought a raw, high-octane energy with their industrial pop-rock entry, “Brutality Mentality.” Bathed in aggressive black and red lighting with flashing LEDs, the performance featured Matthew backed by a live drummer, guitarist, and three dancers. His vocal delivery was gritty and powerful, perfectly matching the song’s driving rhythm and smoke-filled finale.
Having successfully qualified for the Grand Final on January 17, they will perform in the #11 slot. Their unique contribution is a rare, guitar-driven rock presence that injects a bold, rebellious spirit into this year’s competition.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

645.title: MATT BLXCK – Ejja Lejja Ħdejja ‘L Hawn (The Flute)
645.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Matt Blxck electrified the stage with his maximalist ethno-dance entry, “Ejja Lejja Ħdejja ‘L Hawn (The Flute).” His performance was a high-octane showcase featuring a piercing flute hook, thunderous tribal drums, and a charismatic, rapid-fire vocal delivery. Staging was a high-impact “MATT BLXCK Show,” complete with a choreographed dance-break and heavy bass drops.
Successfully qualifying for the Grand Final on January 17, Matt will be the third artist to perform. His unique contribution lies in his infectious energy and the seamless integration of Maltese lyrics into a modern, club-ready anthem.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

657.title: Mark Anthony Bartolo – Mumenti Sbieħ
657.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Mark Anthony Bartolo delivered a “magical” and emotional performance of “Mumenti Sbieħ.” This mid-tempo ballad, written during a songwriting camp, uses the sun as a metaphor for positive memories amidst hardship. Mark Anthony’s vocal delivery was lauded by critics for being even stronger live than on the studio track, conveying a captivating sincerity. The staging was described as “a vibe,” focusing on an authentic, less-choreographed approach that allowed the singer to simply express himself.
Successfully qualifying for the Grand Final on January 17, Mark Anthony will perform in the #9 slot, standing out for his commitment to a fully Maltese-language entry.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

641.title: Janice Mangion – Univers
641.text:
Janice Mangion solidified her reputation as a powerhouse during the MESC 2026 semi-final with “Univers”. Her performance was a cinematic masterclass, blending the “grounded, earthy power” of her vocals with a grand orchestral arrangement. Standing out as a standard-bearer for the Maltese language, she transitioned seamlessly from an intimate, melancholic opening to a soaring, brass-led climax.
This commanding vocal tour-de-force resonated with both the jury and the public, securing her place in the Grand Final. Opening the final, Janice continues to bridge traditional emotional storytelling with modern, high-stakes Eurovision production.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

653.title: Franklin Calleja – Guide you home
653.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Franklin Calleja delivered a vocally impeccable performance of the cinematic ballad “Guide You Home.” Dressed in white, Calleja began the set in front of a mirror before moving forward to be joined by two violinists. His delivery focused on his signature high tenor range, culminating in a dramatic key change and a powerful, sustained high note. The staging, bathed in bright lights and finished with fireworks, emphasized the song’s anthemic, “stadium-ready” quality.
Having qualified for the Grand Final on January 17, Franklin will be the seventh artist, offering a classic, high-caliber vocal showcase.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

643.title: Kelsie Borg – Let a Girl Breathe
643.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Kelsie Borg delivered a high-energy performance of “Let a Girl Breathe.” This sassy, mid-tempo club anthem showcased a modern blend of 90s R&B, funk, and K-pop sensibilities. Her vocal delivery was rhythmic and punchy, emphasized by a catchy “breath” sample and heavy EDM production.
On stage, Borg exuded “star power” during a standout bridge where the music dropped out, spotlighting her personality. Successfully qualifying for the Grand Final on January 17, she will be the second to perform bringing a fresh, contemporary pop direction to this year’s competition.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

647.title: Denise – Trophy
647.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Denise captivated the audience with a polished performance of “Trophy.” This sleek, contemporary electro-pop track featured a mid-tempo groove and sophisticated production. Denise delivered emotional, gentle verses that transitioned into a soulful melodic peak, showcasing her impressive upper register. Her staging was marked by its maturity, mirroring the “radio-ready” quality of the song.
Having successfully qualified for the Grand Final on January 17, Denise will be the fourth artist to perform. Her entry stands out as a refined example of modern pop, blending technical vocal control with high-caliber international appeal.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

651.title: Ema – Achikuku (Don’t think about it)
651.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Ema delivered a vibrant performance of “Achikuku (Don’t Think About It).” This bright, disco-pop track stood out as a “palette cleanser,” featuring infectious African beats and a playful kalimba melody. On stage, Ema’s energy was contagious as she performed in a pink outfit alongside four dancers, creating a colorful atmosphere with moving lights. Her vocal delivery was both cheerful and technically strong, turning the rhythmic chant into a danceable highlight.
Successfully qualifying for the Grand Final on January 17, Ema will be the sixth artist to perform, bringing a refreshing and positive vibe to the competition.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

659.title: AIDAN – Bella
659.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Aidan delivered a cinematic masterclass with his entry “Bella.” Opening the night of January 15, his performance transitioned from a minimalist, light-focused beginning to a dramatic climax flooded with rose petals. The song, a jazzy, 1950s-inspired orchestral pop ballad, showcased Aidan’s flawless live vocals and artistic maturity. Blending English, Maltese, and Italian, the entry highlights his versatile range and deep roots.
Successfully qualifying for the Grand Final on January 17, Aidan will perform in the #10 slot. His unique contribution is a sophisticated, “mushketeer-pop” style that stands out as a timeless contender.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

663.title: Adria Twins – Nerġa’ Nqum
663.text:
In the MESC 2026 semi-final, Adria Twins delivered a powerful and ritualistic performance of the mid-tempo power-pop ballad “Nerġa’ Nqum.” Singing in Maltese, the duo showcased synchronized vocal harmonies that began over a minimalist piano intro before building into a percussion-driven hymn. Their staging utilized dramatic digital distortion and heavy vocal processing during a high-drama bridge, creating a modern, experimental atmosphere.
Having successfully qualified for the Grand Final on January 17, Adria Twins will close the show in the #12 slot. Their entry stands out for its unique “ritualistic” energy and seamless blend of traditional language with digital-age production.
📸 – Albert Camilleri
© Public Broadcasting Services

635.title: PBS Statement
635.text:
Following a query raised by Rhiannon Micallef after her semi-final performance, PBS addressed the matter promptly and with care. PBS met with the singer and members of Rhiannon Micallef’s artistic team to listen carefully to the concerns raised and to review the performance together.
Following comprehensive technical checks and assessments, no production-side technical fault or audio malfunction was identified or substantiated.
The situation was assessed in line with established procedures and the applicable Contest Rules. On this basis, there was no justification for authorising a repeat performance. As a general principle, a repeat performance may only be considered in exceptional circumstances where a verified technical failure has occurred and has materially affected the performance. Any such decision is taken on a case-by-case basis following confirmation by the relevant technical and production teams.
PBS remains committed to treating all performers with respect and to ensuring fairness, transparency, and consistency in the application of the Contest Rules.

626.text:

607.title: DESTINY, GAIA, AND KEANE TO UNVEIL A NEW ERA OF MUSICAL NOSTALGIA
607.text:
Public Broadcasting Services is thrilled to announce the return of the Malta Eurovision Song Contest for 2026, promising an edition filled with vocal power, national pride, and “tons of surprises.”
This year’s national selection will be guided by a powerhouse trio of hosts who represent the very best of Maltese talent. Taking the stage to lead the festivities are popular broadcaster Keane Cutajar and Malta’s two Eurovision icons: Junior Eurovision winner and powerhouse vocalist Destiny Chukunyere, and Junior Eurovision champion Gaia Cauchi. Together, they bring a perfect blend of charisma, experience, and Eurovision legacy to the biggest stage in the country.
The theme for the 2026 edition is ‘L-ewwel lejla li ħabbejt’ (You never forget your first). This evocative theme celebrates the deep-rooted nostalgia and the instant spark of falling in love with music, the stage, and the magic of the Eurovision Song Contest itself. Whether it is a first performance or the first time a fan hears a winning melody, this year’s contest focuses on those unforgettable moments that stay in our hearts forever.
Fans can expect a high-octane production featuring the finest artists in the Maltese music scene, all vying for the honor of representing Malta on the international stage. The journey to find our next representative will unfold over two spectacular live shows:
The Semi-Final: Thursday, 15th January 2026
The Grand Final: Saturday, 17th January 2026
The energy of the MESC is best experienced live! Audience members will be treated to world-class performances, stunning visuals, and exclusive surprises that will only be revealed on the night.
Tickets are available now at:
https://www.showshappening.com/Public-Broadcasting-Services-Limited/Malta-Eurovision-Song-Contest-2026
Join us this January as we celebrate ‘L-ewwel lejla li ħabbejt’ and discover who will carry the Maltese flag to the world stage!

1071.title: Ready, set, write: the road to Eurovision 2027 starts now
1071.text:
The wait is over. PBS has published the official Rules & Regulations for the Malta Eurovision Song Contest 2027, the first step on Malta’s road to Eurovision 2027.
Got a song? This is your moment.
Submissions open on Wednesday 9 December and close on Wednesday 23 December 2026. Every entry goes through the official submission link on maltaeurovision.mt, and entering is completely free.
Three minutes. One shot. Make it count.
Songs can run up to three minutes, and they must be brand new: no part of the song may have been released, shared or performed in public before it’s submitted.
Made in Malta, made for Europe.
Lead vocalists must be Maltese or have lived in Malta for the 24 months before 1 May 2027. At least one songwriter must be Maltese or live in Malta, and every performer must be 18 or over by the first Eurovision 2027 rehearsal.
Real voices only.
Everything is sung live: no lip-syncing, and no Auto-Tune on stage. Wholly AI-generated songs, lyrics or performances are not eligible.
18 songs. 12 finalists. One ticket to Burgas.
A professional jury picks 18 songs for the Semi-Final on Friday 29 January 2027, and the semi-finalists are announced on Monday 4 January. The jury and the public vote together to send 12 of them to the Grand Final on Saturday 30 January.
The prize? The biggest stage in Europe.
The winner flies Malta’s flag at the Eurovision Song Contest 2027 in Burgas, Bulgaria, where the Eurovision Final is on Saturday 15 May 2027. The winner also receives €25,000 towards their Eurovision journey, plus a full PBS support package: the official music video, staging, styling and creative direction.
Key dates
